initialPrompts.dark:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high fidelity, shippable desktop developer-tool UI concept for LAZERS, an OpenCode Desktop plugin. This is a product design mockup with illustrative task data. Precise, readable English text and crisp vector-like UI rendering, not a photograph or poster. Linear-like dense task list, understated system sans typography, compact mono task IDs, hairline separators, restrained status colors with icons and text, 4px spacing rhythm, 36px task rows. No kanban, no dependency node graph, no KPI cards, no gradients, no marketing copy. The user cares about task visibility and truthful runtime status.
Composition: landscape desktop application screenshot at approximately 1800x1200. OpenCode outer chrome and a slim left session sidebar. A conversation column occupies roughly 35% of the remaining width, and an open native LAZERS Tasks side panel occupies 65%. Within Tasks, a horizontal resizable divider creates a top list region (52% height) and a bottom selected-task inspector (48%). The plugin looks integrated into the host, using its typography, surfaces, small buttons, tabs, icons. Never make a floating web dashboard in the app. Thin top tab strip has "Tasks" active and "System" inactive. LAZERS wordmark is tiny plain text, no invented logo.
Tasks header: "Tasks" then tiny connection dot + "Live". Scope control "opencode-lazers", search field "Find tasks…", filter "Active", grouping control "Feature", quiet "History". One small "Needs input 1" control. Accepted/completed tasks hidden by Active filter; eight open task rows. A small quiet line reads "8 active · 3 accepted hidden". Grouping by feature with expandable group headers, nested rows, state icon, mono ID, concise title, state text, and a compact dependency/scheduling reason at right. Parallelism is indicated by an understated bracket or shared "Parallel A" marker on two sibling rows, sequential dependencies by "After LZ-101" badges. Do not draw graph connector arrows across the screen.
Group 1 header "Retry-safe submission" with "2 running · 3 waiting".
Rows exact:
"LZ-101" "Persist submission identity" "Running" "Parallel A"
"LZ-102" "Document retry contract" "Running" "Parallel A"
"LZ-103" "Exercise restart recovery" "Ready" "After LZ-101" [this row selected]
"LZ-104" "Verify native tool replay" "Ready" "After LZ-101"
"LZ-105" "Accept submission increment" "Ready" "After 3 tasks"
Group 2 header "Task visibility" with "1 repairing · 2 waiting".
"LZ-106" "Resolve grouping semantics" "Draft" "Needs input"
"LZ-107" "Render task inspector" "Draft" "After LZ-106"
"LZ-108" "Restore live subscriptions" "Repairing" "Attempt 1/1"
Bottom inspector selected task LZ-103 title "Exercise restart recovery", small "Ready" state and "Revision 2". Separate readiness reason on next line: "Waiting for LZ-101 · Persist submission identity". Tabs "Overview" active, "Acceptance", "Activity". The selected task is not running. Show concise objective: "A fresh process retries a lost submission receipt and returns the original task ID." Relations in one compact row: "Depends on LZ-101" "Unblocks LZ-105" "Can run with LZ-104". Visible acceptance preview checklist: "Original ID established from committed storage" and "Fresh process returns same ID; one task remains". These are requirements with empty circles, NOT passed checks. Metadata line "Attempt —   Worker not assigned   Budget 12k tokens / $1.20". Scope line "test/submission-retry-worker.ts · src/storage.test.ts". Bottom tiny activity preview "02:18  Specification revised by Architect" and understated "Open specification" and "Ask Architect" links. Header action menu for further runtime actions, no giant approval button, no fake success statistics. Footer of inspector "Evidence not produced". Distinguish state from scheduling readiness.
The subdued conversation column shows Architect with two short messages and a compact native tool receipt, e.g. "The plan is scoped. Two independent tasks can run together; restart and tool checks follow the storage change." and "5 tasks submitted". Composer at bottom "Ask Architect…" with model "GPT-6.1 Sol · High". Avoid lengthy chat transcription.
No explanatory labels outside the application. Accurate text hierarchy, subtle selected row, generous enough column alignment to prevent overlaps.
Variant: DARK DOCKED VIEW. OpenCode host currently uses a very dark indigo-charcoal background, a slightly elevated charcoal-violet conversation surface, muted cool gray secondary text, near-white primary text, and a subdued periwinkle selection accent. Match that host visual language. No glow. The task panel shares the host surface. Selected LZ-103 row has a faint blue-violet tint and a thin left accent. Running blue, Repairing muted amber, Draft neutral; Needs input amber with icon. Smooth Mac app chrome, compact rounded corners only on small controls. Render the whole application readable at desktop scale.

Variant: LIGHT EXPANDED INSPECTOR VIEW. Same underlying product and information architecture with a neutral light OpenCode theme: very pale warm-neutral page, white/pale gray panel surfaces, charcoal primary text, gray secondary text, subdued blue selection accent. Keep all task IDs, names, counts, statuses, relationships and selected row identical. Make the side panel slightly wider and show "Acceptance" as the active inspector tab instead of Overview. Beneath the same selected-task header and readiness reason, show two numbered acceptance assertions, each with explicit required evidence and no passed indicators: "1  Retry survives a host process restart" with "Fresh subprocess, same key and content, original task ID"; "2  No duplicate task is created" with "Exactly one task and key binding in committed storage". Small artifact placeholder "Evidence pending". A collapsed section "Full specification · scope, limits, context" and a bottom activity line "Specification revised by Architect". Keep relationships visible. Include a quiet outlined chip "Theme follows OpenCode" in the outer host top bar, not an independent plugin theme selector. The mockup demonstrates coherent light styling, not a separate redesign. Dense rows, quiet divider and no cards.

refinements.prompt: Edit this UI mockup surgically. Preserve its entire layout, content, palette, spacing, row counts and all other pixels as closely as possible. Correct only two labels: in the selected task's Relations row, change 'Can run with LZ-194' to exactly 'Can run with LZ-104'. In the LZ-108 task row, ensure the status is spelled exactly 'Repairing' (R e p a i r i n g). No other changes.
refinements.outcome: Discarded; small relationship label was not reliably corrected.

refinements.prompt: Edit this light-theme LAZERS/OpenCode UI mockup into the corresponding dark-theme mockup. Preserve every task, ID, label, count, column, relationship, selected row, panel proportion, all control placements, and the active Acceptance tab exactly. Change only the theme to the current OpenCode visual language: very dark indigo-charcoal base, slightly lifted charcoal surfaces, near-white primary text, cool gray secondary text, muted periwinkle selection and focus. Use semantic running/repairing colors with readable text. Every surface must be flat and quiet with subtle separators, no gradient or glow. Preserve exact relationship label 'Can run with LZ-104' and exact task status 'Repairing'. Do not invent navigation or content. This is the dark appearance of the same plugin UI, not a redesign.
